text:
maria: Heads up — noticed p95 jump on /v1/generate for endpoint foo-prod after yesterday's variant suppression rollout. p50/p95 moved up but p99 barely changed. Screenshot: https://redwood.screens/abc123
aj: can you paste the raw numbers?
maria: p50 45ms -> 52ms, p95 210ms -> 340ms, p99 720ms -> 730ms (sample counts: 18k -> 9k)
sam: wow p95 doubled but p99 flat — smells like sampling bias due to suppressed variant A (was low-latency)
jonathan: confirm: variant A had client-side affinity, and we reduced its weight to 0.1 in routing policy for the canary?
maria: yes, config change: `routing.v1.foo.variantA.weight=0.1` rolled yesterday 22:14 UTC (canary).
aj: when weight goes down expected overall latency might increase, but p99 staying same suggests p99 was dominated by slow tail from other variants pre-change and counts halved so p95 moved.
sam: dashboard is currently aggregating percentiles from sampled per-variant tdigest merge; with smaller sample for some variants the interpolation shifts — need to show origin of samples in UI
maria: users confused — UI shows endpoint-level p50/p95/p99 with no provenance. Product asked why p95 jumped while p99 didn't.
jonathan: two threads here: (1) telemetry correctness (we must surface sample origins & counts), (2) UX: how to avoid surprising product owners.
aj: proposal: add a small badge next to each percentile like `[p95 · 9k samples · origin: merged]` and hover shows per-variant breakdown.
maria: also add a warning when the effective sample rate changed >30% in the window: `Sample rate down — percentiles may be unstable`
sam: agree. Also consider showing aggregated vs raw tdigest merge mode toggle. Right now merge uses weighted tdigest which can obscure small-variant influence.
jonathan: on the infra side we should ensure the API returns both merged percentiles and per-variant prototype percentiles in the metrics API: `GET /metrics/latency?endpoint=foo-prod&window=5m&mode=both`
aj: debating internal API surface — do we return arrays of {variant, count, p50,p95,p99} or keep compact and rely on tags? returning arrays is clearer for UI but heavier on payloads.
sam: keep both: default compact, and `expand=variants` param to return per-variant time series. consoles can call expand for drilldowns.
maria: product question: what about quota fallbacks? Some requests were routed to a lower-tier pool when weight dipped and that pool had a higher e2e processing time, could contribute to p95 shift.
jonathan: good catch — routing policy fallback logs show spikes in `quota.fallback=true` around same time. We should tag those samples and surface a filter "exclude quota-fallback" in console for debugging.
aj: quick mitigation: add provenance dot on percentile widget that links to a precomputed breakdown and shows `breakdown: variant weights, quota-fallback %, samplecounts`
maria: UX request: when an endpoint percentile changes >X% and samplecount changed >Y, open a rollout-auto-note linking to the policy change so ownership gets alerted automatically.
sam: implementation note: our tdigest rollups can't represent sample origin metadata. We'll need to augment rollup rows with `origin_tags: {variant:<id>, fallback:bool}` and keep a lightweight counters index for the window.
jonathan: also worth adding a small regression test in the telemetry pipeline: simulate weight shift and assert p50/p95 move monotically in expected direction given variant latencies.
aj: action items: 1) UI badge + hover + expand per-variant (owner: maria) 2) metrics API `expand=variants` (owner: sam) 3) tag quota-fallback in samples & add filter (owner: jonathan) 4) alert rule prototype for large percentile+sample deltas (owner: aj)
maria: thanks — I'll draft a console mock and drop in #design tomorrow.
console-bot: Note: rollout canary at 22:14 UTC recorded by rollout-service (id: r-2026-03-22-77).
deploy-bot: Deployed telemetry change branch `pctl-provenance-annotate` to staging at 11:05 UTC — will run synthetic tonight. :rocket:
aj: pinging on PRs. If we can ship the badge and expand param this sprint we might avoid more "why p95 jumped" DMs to product.
maria: agree. will start with minimal badge + link.
sam: one more thought — add a little info icon that explains why p95 could move while p99 doesn't (sampling math blurb). Can write a short paragraph.
jonathan: perfect. thanks team!
